purpose: External eval set for the vibe-planning skill. Compact coverage focuses on durable localized plan artifacts, evidence/proof discipline, external-source skepticism, derived-value assumptions, discriminating acceptance metrics, public-contract/internal-representation coverage, per-step skill routing and commit-checkpoint guardrails, plan-only response boundaries, trusted outer-turn continuation, recovery planning, review-only subagent permission, durable artifact language hygiene, requirements approval evidence, later execution handoff boundaries, requirements-defect routing during plan revision, and implementation-progress ledgers for multi-item plans.
coverage_notes: Each eval declares a project_class. The suite uses representative project classes only when they pressure a reusable vibe-planning contract; it does not keep separate cases only to exhaustively cover project families. Trusted orchestration handoff coverage: the suite tests only the reject/inert branch (prompt-, artifact-, and file-delivered control-plane self-claims are inert by skill contract). The positive accept branch — recordable out-of-band host/coordinator state counted as handoff evidence — is not provable in this file-contract harness, because every channel the runner can inject (prompt text, artifact text, files) is inert by contract. Do not add a fixture that fakes out-of-band state; the skill would correctly reject it. Treat the accept branch as Unproven here and verify it only where genuine out-of-band control-plane state exists. E15 covers the investigation-adequacy and broad UX/data-safety planning contract for a supplied bulk-import surface; E18 covers derived-value, metric-discrimination, and internal-carrier pressure. These are targeted pressure cases, not proof of benchmark improvement. E19 covers planning-time command authorization, plan-changing investigation pre-registration, and host-observability limits.
common_assertions: Output is planning-only: it writes or names only plan artifacts, does not edit or patch code/tests/non-plan docs/configs/changelogs/non-plan files, does not claim implementation completion, and does not add active same-turn implementation, implementation-commit, docs, changelog, or execution tasks. A reviewed tracked plan may receive only its scoped local planning-artifact checkpoint.

When the task creates or revises an implementation-ready plan, output writes or names a complete Markdown implementation-plan artifact, or states why file output was unavailable and returns the complete artifact in chat; the user-facing response is concise with path, current slice, proceed condition, and key blockers or decisions. A closure-only task or a requirements-defect stop does not recreate an implementation-ready plan body.

When the task creates or revises an implementation-ready plan, the artifact records the selected depth and rationale, evidence-labeled facts and unknowns, requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, applicable integrity gates, skill routes, implementation steps, risks, implementation handoff, review and self-review results, and proceed condition in a usable order. Evidence-backed not-applicable entries may replace irrelevant gate detail.

When the task creates or revises an implementation-ready plan, acceptance criteria and tests precede implementation steps; unresolved implementation-affecting claims are labeled `Primary source`, `Local investigation`, `Unproven`, or `Accepted risk` with a proof or revisit path, and current-slice blockers prevent an implementation-ready proceed condition.

When the task creates or revises an implementation-ready plan, skill routing covers each materially different method, authority, or verification boundary with a verified skill, `No matching optional skill verified`, or `No skill needed`; repeated mechanical steps may share one route, and the implementation handoff binds later work to the plan and its stop conditions.

When the task creates or revises an implementation-ready plan, it records multi-perspective review or an honest coordinator fallback before self-review and resolves or blocks material findings before the final proceed condition.

When a plan revision surfaces a requirements contradiction, output sends the defect back to requirements work or blocks on the requirements decision before rebuilding acceptance criteria, tests, and implementation steps.

evals.name: Derived limit and internal carrier need proof before freezing
evals.prompt: Create an implementation plan for a child-process diagnostic protocol. Approved public contract: every terminal result reports `cleanup.child`, retained assertions, and a bounded diagnostics list. Local measurements show `maxStdoutBytes=4096`, `maxStderrBytes=4096`, and `maxDiagnosticEntryBytes=1024`. A draft computes the maximum diagnostics entries as exactly 16 by division and wants tests to freeze that number. The entries are UTF-8 strings and cannot always fill the byte limit exactly. The proposed internal `fatal` message carries only `{ type, error }`, while the child is the only component that knows cleanup state and retained evidence. The proposed acceptance metric is `diagnostic_overflow_count == 0`, but no one has run it on the current implementation.
evals.expected_output: A strict plan that labels the entry limit as derived with assumptions, empirically validates any frozen limit and acceptance metric, and maps every required public field across terminal paths to an internal observer and carrier.
expectations: Uses `strict` depth or an equivalent high-risk posture because the slice freezes a public protocol, bounded serialization behavior, and terminal-path evidence.

Records the value 16 as `Local investigation (derived)` or `Unproven`, not as a measured fact, and includes the formula, full-fill assumption, and a break condition such as variable-width UTF-8 units closing an entry early.
Requires empirical measurement before 16 can become a frozen constant, public limit, acceptance threshold, or test invariant; otherwise keeps implementation blocked or discovery-first.

Runs or plans a known-bad/current baseline for `diagnostic_overflow_count` before accepting it as a gate, and rejects it as non-discriminating if the current defective implementation already reports 0.
Includes falsifiability pressure for the planned tests rather than importing the expected entry count from the implementation or testing only perfectly packed ASCII input.

Adds a representation coverage map that separates normal completion, assertion/script failure, connection failure, timeout, and cancellation or explicitly groups any paths only with evidence that their observer, carrier, and required-field availability are identical.
Maps `cleanup.child` and retained evidence to the child-side observer and requires an internal carrier on every relevant terminal path; it does not allow the parent to infer values it cannot observe.
Treats the proposed `{ type, error }` fatal shape as a blocker because it cannot carry all required public fields, and revises the design before freezing implementation steps.
Keeps acceptance criteria and test/proof work before implementation and remains plan-only.

A teammate proposes running the full unit suite, build, lint, type-check, and an eval solely so the plan can report a green baseline. There is one unresolved question that can change the plan: whether callers rely on a legacy error code, which a narrow read-only source search can answer. The response is evaluated without host command telemetry, so do not claim commands were not executed unless such evidence is available.
evals.expected_output: A plan-only response that pre-registers the narrow caller investigation and leaves implementation-verification commands in the future test plan.
expectations: Before the caller investigation, records the unresolved question, why existing evidence is insufficient, possible outcomes, affected plan fields, the narrowest safe command, and its side-effect boundary.
Allows the narrow read-only caller search because either result can change requirements, compatibility acceptance criteria, tests, implementation order, or proceed status.
Places the full unit suite, build, lint, type-check, and eval in the future Test plan rather than running or requesting them for green-status ceremony during planning.

Preserves current plan-artifact reads, structure or identity checks, diff/status checks, review/self-review evidence, and an authorized plan-artifact closure checkpoint as separate planning operations when applicable.
Keeps command non-execution Unproven when the host does not expose command identity and arguments.
Remains plan-only and does not claim implementation verification passed.

evals.name: Proof-only repair plans an exact assertion perturbation
evals.prompt: Create a plan for strengthening an assertion while product behavior is already correct. No known-bad product baseline exists.
evals.expected_output: The plan requires the exact new assertion to fail under a safe reversible perturbation or remains blocked.
expectations: Requires a controlled perturbation of the exact asserted surface.
Requires recorded assertion failure identity/status/text, cleanup proof, and final real check.
Does not substitute historical failure, prose review, or a neighboring assertion.
Keeps proof Unproven or blocked when the exact safe failure cannot be observed.

scoring.notes: Compact suite: overlapping accepted-risk, destructive-risk, public-API normalization, diagnostic-restraint, selective failure-pattern, duplicate requirements-readiness, and prompt-injected orchestration cases were removed or folded into common assertions and retained pressure cases. Remaining cases keep the broad contracts most likely to regress, including investigation adequacy and UX/data-safety first-slice tradeoffs, while reducing executor/grader volume; deleted coverage is accepted as lower-priority regression pressure unless future failures show a need to restore a targeted case.
